extensions.description: Phase 55 02.5: the canary member record of each tenant: an id no membership has and no list, report or export shows (derived from the server's field key, never stored). /api/members/<id> answers it as any missing member; asking for it is a critical signal about the signed-in caller.

extensionPoints.description: A header button of the Members page (/admin/members) that opens another module's panel in a right-side drawer, as the Devices page opens "Awaiting approval (n)": "Invitations (n)" (tenant_invitation, the pending invitations). The sidebar has no item for it (docs/phases/45-install-config, owner 2026-10-27). Implemented through the CLIENT slot 'tenant_member.members.drawers': a contributor declares slots[] = { slot: 'tenant_member.members.drawers', component, order, scope: 'tenant', permissions, props: { drawerId, label, labelKey } }; the component default-exports a function of { tenantId, open, onCount, onClose } (common/ui/slot-drawers.component). It stays mounted while its drawer is shut, draws its panel only while open, and may report the number its button shows through onCount. The page shows a button only when its module is on and the viewer holds its permissions, isolates each in an error boundary, and opens the drawer whose drawerId is in `?tab=` on arrival (the old tab's link, /admin/members?tab=invitations). tenant_member imports none of the contributors (EXT-14).

failOpen.reason: A quota guard: an unavailable reservation source undercounts reserved seats, so an invite may pass a plan limit; refusing every invite because a contributor broke is the worse failure (EXT-3).

extensionPoints.description: A holder of seats that are spoken for but not yet ACTIVE members. Default export: { countReserved(tenantId) } implementing SeatReservationProvider. Consulted at ISSUE time — when a tenant adds a member or sends an invitation — so the plan's `max_members` ceiling counts unclaimed seats too; without it a tenant could issue unlimited invitations under the cap and let every acceptance walk in unchecked. A contributor that throws is treated as zero rather than refusing the operation: an unrelated module's outage must not look like a billing refusal. Declared so `tenant_member`, the primitive invitations are built on, never imports them back.

A ready-made custom group a tenant can add in one click (Access control > Groups > From template). Default export: { key (lowercase role key), label, description?, permissions: string[] }. Contributions with the SAME key merge, and each module lists only its OWN permissions (e.g. commerce_order + commerce_fulfillment + commerce_return + commerce_review make store_operator). Offered permissions are filtered to the tenant's enabled modules, and a template left empty is not offered. Exists because lowering a permission's minRole to USER also grants it to every storefront shopper (sign-up makes them USER members); a group grants it only to the staff it is assigned to.

Told after a member stops being an ACTIVE member of a workspace (removed, suspended, deprovisioned), with { tenantId, userId, reason, sessionEndOrderedBy? } (D249: the modules whose session_end:order_source orders the membership's own transaction already recorded; their hooks skip it). Default export: (ended) => Promise<void>. For things addressed to the person because they were a member and that must stop the moment they are not — notification_push deletes their push registrations for the workspace, otherwise a removed member's phone keeps receiving the workspace's notifications. Best-effort by contract: a hook that throws is logged and skipped, removing someone must never fail because a satellite's cleanup had trouble.

Told after an ACTIVE member's built-in role or custom roles changed, with { tenantId, userId, reason: 'role' | 'role_keys', sessionEndOrderedBy? } (D249, as membership_ended). Default export: (changed) => Promise<void>. For things granted once and kept that must follow the new rights: websocket_session drops the member's sockets in the workspace so they come back with tickets minted under the new role (websocket.08). Ending a membership is tenant_member:membership_ended. Best-effort by contract: a hook that throws is logged and skipped.

A ceiling on the number of members beyond the plan's `max_members` limit: the seats a tenant's entitlements include, with the admin override. Default export: { effectiveLimit(tenantId) => Promise<number | null> } implementing SeatAllowanceProvider; null states no ceiling. Consulted when a member is added, where the tightest ceiling of all contributors applies. Declared so `tenant_member`, the tenancy primitive, never imports the module that sells seats.
